correctness.rationale: At every convex tangent polygon vertex, the two outgoing tangency segments have lengths tan x_i, with half exterior angle x_i∈(0,π/2) and ∑x_i=π. Total k retained side lengths are weighted convex objective F=tan x1+tan x_{k+1}+2∑_{i=2}^{k}tan x_i. Strict convexity of tan on positive half interval plus Lagrange multipliers give endpoints a, others b, sec²a=2sec²b, and unique interior root, hence unique global optimum (including boundary infima). Adjacent normal gaps 2x_i give a valid strictly convex circumscribed polygon. Splitting any interior angle b halves its contribution with 4tan(b/2)<2tan b, proving strict improvement in k. At q=k−1, Taylor solve b=π/(2q)+O(q^-3), a=π/4+b²/2+O(b4), giving L_k=π+2+π³/(12q²)+O(q^-4). Projection of connected chain is an interval equal to its convex-hull projection, and its convex hull is the circumscribed polygon containing the disk, hence it hits every disk-intersecting line. Independent constrained SLSQP minimization k=2..11 recovers the angle pattern, exact k2/k3 and asymptotic trend.

originality.rationale: The classical connected-disk opaque barrier benchmark π+2 and theories of curves whose convex hull covers a disk are prior, and a minimum Hamiltonian path of the vertices of a *fixed* convex polygon does not solve simultaneous optimization of variable tangent side angles at prescribed k. Full Dumitrescu–Jiang–Pach Opaque sets and accessible Nikonorov descriptions lack this specific equal-two-endpoint and shared-interior-angle optimization. Faber–Mycielski–Pedersen (1984), the strongest historical connected-disk-barrier paper, was inaccessible in full even after authorized attempt; no whole-document noncoverage is asserted. Best-of-knowledge PASS with this specific residual risk.
residual_risks: Faber–Mycielski–Pedersen original 1984 circle-barrier paper may contain essentially the same finite-link tangential-polygon problem or stronger finite-link optimization; publisher and authorized institutional full text unavailable.
The optimizer is unique only inside strictly convex (k+1)-gons circumscribed about the disk with one side removed; no claim for arbitrary k-link connected barriers.
The approach toward π+2 is an asymptotic benchmark, not proof of unrestricted exact optimality at finite k.

value.rationale: Finite k connected polygonal barriers provide a natural geometric approximation hierarchy to the classical π+2 connected-disk barrier. Exact classification of all strict convex tangent polygon optimizers at each k, plus the sharp inverse-square excess constant, makes a motivated restricted geometric extremal result. Restriction to tangential polygons with one side omitted is essential, and no unproved unrestricted barrier claim is smuggled in.

final_claim: For every integer k>=2, among chains obtained by deleting exactly one side of a strictly convex unit-circle-circumscribed (k+1)-gon, the minimum retained k-link length is L_k=2tan a_k+2(k-1)tan b_k, uniquely optimized by two equal endpoint half-exterior angles a and k-1 equal interior b satisfying sec²a=2sec²b and 2a+(k-1)b=π. L_2=(1+√5)√(2+√5), L_3=4√2, L_k strictly decreases to π+2 with excess π³/[12(k-1)²]+O(k^-4). Each chain is a connected opaque barrier for the unit disk. No unrestricted k-link optimum is claimed.
limitations: k>=2, unit disk radius one, strict convex circumscribed tangent (k+1)-gon with precisely one omitted side; no arbitrary barrier minimization.
